moc: Old St Paul's Cathedral: very long Gothic nave with a square crossing tower and NO spire (spire lost 1561), NO dome
Old London Bridge lined with houses
NO Wren dome or Wren steeples

ghi_chu.mo_ta: A burning courtyard enclosed by a classical Italian-Renaissance palazzo. It has tiers of round-arched arcades, statues in niches, and rusticated pilasters. This is not a view of London.
ghi_chu.ly_do: The scene is meant to be the Great Fire of London in 1666, but the architecture is Italianate and does not match London buildings of the time. London then had timber-framed houses and Gothic Old St Paul's. Arcaded stone courtyards with rows of niche statues did not exist there.

ghi_chu.mo_ta: The view contains none of the expected 1666 landmarks. Old St Paul's with its Gothic nave and square crossing tower is absent, and so is Old London Bridge with its houses. A Renaissance courtyard stands in their place.
ghi_chu.ly_do: A view of London in 1666 should show Old St Paul's, which was burning in the fire. It is replaced here by a generic classical palazzo.
